Not suggesting you change your approach necessarily, so marking this as resolved to start with.

My approach here has been to use `executable(..., implicit_include_directories: false, ...)`, and then provide an explicit list of include directories, which in this case we'd constrain to `src/`. From there the `#include "..."` directive in each translation unit needs to use the path relative to `src/`, which helps disambiguate. I feel this is helpful because it explicitly aligns the source with the repository's file hierarchy and may remove the need to move everything under `src/common/`.

> and may remove the need to move everything under src/common/.

Maybe you have some extra input here since you know the code much better.

Currently we have `struct Sensor` which is for an individual sensor and for example `class ADCSensor` which inherits from `Sensor`.

But we do not have something like `class SensorManager` or `class SensorReactor` right?
Something to hold the io context and all the other stuff

from ADCSensor
```
int main()
{
    boost::asio::io_context io; 
    auto systemBus = std::make_shared<sdbusplus::asio::connection>(io);
    sdbusplus::asio::object_server objectServer(systemBus, true);
    objectServer.add_manager("/xyz/openbmc_project/sensors");

    systemBus->request_name("xyz.openbmc_project.ADCSensor");
    boost::container::flat_map<std::string, std::shared_ptr<ADCSensor>> sensors;
    auto sensorsChanged =
        std::make_shared<boost::container::flat_set<std::string>>();
```

from HwmonTempSensor
```

int main()
{
    boost::asio::io_context io; 
    auto systemBus = std::make_shared<sdbusplus::asio::connection>(io);
    sdbusplus::asio::object_server objectServer(systemBus, true);
    objectServer.add_manager("/xyz/openbmc_project/sensors");
    systemBus->request_name("xyz.openbmc_project.HwmonTempSensor");

    boost::container::flat_map<std::string, std::shared_ptr<HwmonTempSensor>>
        sensors;
    auto sensorsChanged =
        std::make_shared<boost::container::flat_set<std::string>>();
```

PSUSensor is similar as well.

So we have all this common logic and common variables but nothing to contain it.

Now if someone asks "where do i find the common code", i do not want to say `src`,
i want to say `src/common` and `tests/common`.

If we tell them `src/` ! then it may be overwhelming for that person since there is so many sensors directories in there. So it may be distracting a reader from understanding how the 'generic' sensor code works.

It's also distracting from `meson.build` perspective since we are mixing the building of common code with meson `subdir(...)` calls.

This is how it looks for me
```
[alexander@alexanderarchlinux dbus-sensors]$ ls src/
adc                         FileHandle.hpp     NotifyWatch.cpp  SystemdInterface.cpp
cable-monitor               GPIOInterface.cpp  NotifyWatch.hpp  SystemdInterface.hpp
dbus-sensor_config.h.in     GPIOInterface.hpp  nvidia-gpu       tests
DeviceMgmt.cpp              hwmon-temp         nvme             Thresholds.cpp
DeviceMgmt.hpp              intel-cpu          psu              Thresholds.hpp
EntityManagerInterface.cpp  intrusion          PwmSensor.cpp    Utils.cpp
EntityManagerInterface.hpp  ipmb               PwmSensor.hpp    Utils.hpp
exit-air                    leakdetector       sensor.hpp       VariantVisitors.hpp
external                    mctp               SensorPaths.cpp
fan                         mcu                SensorPaths.hpp
FileHandle.cpp              meson.build        smbpbi
```

when it is actually much smaller

```
[alexander@alexanderarchlinux dbus-sensors]$ ls src/common/
DeviceMgmt.cpp              GPIOInterface.cpp  PwmSensor.hpp         Thresholds.cpp
DeviceMgmt.hpp              GPIOInterface.hpp  sensor.hpp            Thresholds.hpp
EntityManagerInterface.cpp  meson.build        SensorPaths.cpp       Utils.cpp
EntityManagerInterface.hpp  NotifyWatch.cpp    SensorPaths.hpp       Utils.hpp
FileHandle.cpp              NotifyWatch.hpp    SystemdInterface.cpp  VariantVisitors.hpp
FileHandle.hpp              PwmSensor.cpp      SystemdInterface.hpp
```

### include patterns

> feel this is helpful because it explicitly aligns the source with the repository's file hierarchy


Yes but then an ADC sensor reactor will `#include adc/ADCSensor.hpp`, right? 
Which makes it look like it's including a library or something when it's including it's own header.

Making it appear as if it's own header was somehow more distant than the common code.
?  what does "cleaned up" mean here?  The former looks easier to read than the later.

refer to https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#Rs-incform

which has some note on angle brackets an quotes in include statements.

Also if we have some common code it would be good to have a way to tell if we are including common code or some header that's local to a single reactor.
Can you explain this so I understand what it means?

`Inventory` sounds like that's some common header which is to be used by various reactors.

If we have no way to tell via the `#include` statement if it's a common header or local to a specific reactor then it can be confusing to the reader.

Another way to solve this would be to rename it to `NvidiaInventory.hpp`.

Looking to see what other people say about this.  I don't find this organization easier to use than what we've got given the current scale of things.  I'd much rather we go more specific folders like

asio
reactor

that can match the appropriate namespaces rather than just having one common folder for everything.  Looking forward to what other people think, but blanket rearranging this when the code that's underneath it is already pretty manageable seems like a lot of effort for very little gain.

@alexander.hansen@9elements.com As a first cut probably we can move the files into their subsequent buckets which doesn't have to be concretely based on absolute namespace. Probably something as under -

reactor -  (asynchronus method agnostic common code for all reactors)
* SensorPaths.hpp
* SensorPaths.cpp

asio
* DeviceMgmt.hpp
* DeviceMgmt.cpp
* Thresholds.hpp
* Thresholds.cpp
* PwmSensor.cpp
* PwmSensor.hpp

async_task -
* EntityManagerInterface.cpp
* EntityManagerInterface.hpp
* GPIOInterface.cpp
* GPIOInterface.hpp
* NotifyWatch.cpp
* NotifyWatch.hpp
* SystemdInterface.hpp
* SystemdInterface.cpp

utils -
* Utils.cpp
* Utils.hpp
* VariantVisitors.hpp
* FileHandle.cpp
* FileHandle.hpp  << This only provides a RAII wrapper for fd, so seems better in utils

For header inclusion, we can probably choose <dir>/<filename.hpp> related inclusion for outside (from local dir) to give some hint on where the header is being included from.

Would let others comment about their feedback.

Looks reasonable to me 👍. Thanks for the detailed list.

Split it into 

`asio/`, `async_task/` and `utils/` since `utils/` 
code already builds together,
so i did not want to separate the `SensorPaths.cpp` from the others.

This way we keep this patch to a restructuring of files into folders and not introduce a restructuring of build targets at the same time.

Why is this in asio?  This doesn't appear to pull in any asio headers.

Looks like it's header does, as per your other comment https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/83895/comment/9244a824_132cd9c0/

`${name}.cpp` and `${name}.hpp` files go in the same folder in dbus-sensors. Are you implying we should change that?

That would be an even bigger work.
This file really needs broken out.  Every utility except for this one has nothing to do with asio, so overall this really shouldn't go into a common asio folder.

You are introducing scope creep to this restructuring.

Can we not do a coarse grained restructuring first and then worry about functions which are in the wrong file?

We are already at roughly -300/+300 for this simple coarse grained restructuring.

Do you want me to stack a patch on top for breaking out that function into a separate file?

Can you let me know what's to be the name of that file and where it should go?
This is a specific daemon implementation, this should not be put into a common folder.
It's shared by both `fan` and `psu` reactors so i assume this is a common code?
Should we call the folder sdbusplus_context ?  "async_task" could arguably apply to asio as well.

I don't see a problem with `async_task`. If we have an `asio` folder then that already tells us where the boost asio stuff goes. 

sdbusplus has
`include/sdbusplus/asio/`
and 
`include/sdbusplus/async`

so there is somewhat of a precendent regarding the directory names.

If we go with that direction then it will better match with what's in sdbusplus.

I went with `async_task` because that's the name of the template used for the functions.

Since you worded your comment as a question i assume you are open to change your mind here. Let me know if it's a strong preference.

This kind of thing is why I don't find this organization better.  "utils" is repeated, and doesn't add additional value.  We can argue the Utils.hpp shouldn't exist, but that's not what we have today.

lets get this file list removed for now so we can get this approved in concept, and see if we can restructure a little bit to make this not a list of files. (i'm open to options on what that looks like, and there's some discussion already on alexanders review).
